validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, FERC-certificated feed-gas pipeline serving the Commonwealth LNG LNG-export terminal, Cameron Parish, Louisiana. Commonwealth LNG, LLC filed its NGA application with FERC on Aug 20, 2019 (Docket CP19-502-000; Federal Register notice of application, https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2019/09/09/2019-19428/commonwealth-lng-llc-notice-of-application, published 2019-09-09, restating the Aug 20, 2019 filing date). FERC's Final EIS news release (Wayback capture of ferc.gov, https://web.archive.org/web/20220909160655/https://www.ferc.gov/news-events/news/ferc-staff-issues-final-environmental-impact-statement-commonwealth-lng-project) and FERC's own project-directory page (Wayback capture, https://web.archive.org/web/20250321182833/https://www.ferc.gov/commonwealth-lng-project) both describe the authorized facilities as '3.0 miles of 42-inch-diameter pipeline ... to provide approximately 1.44 billion cubic feet per day of natural gas to the LNG terminal.' Direct fetches of ferc.gov returned HTTP 403 (bot-blocked); Wayback snapshots were used instead per the escalation rule and both passed url_verifier.py. Independent trade-press corroboration: offshore-technology.com (https://www.offshore-technology.com/projects/commonwealth-lng-terminal-louisiana-usa/) and S&P Global Commodity Insights' contemporaneous Aug 2019 filing article (direct fetch 403'd; Wayback capture used, https://web.archive.org/web/20220420001722/https://www.spglobal.com/commodityinsights/en/market-insights/latest-news/natural-gas/082019-commonwealth-lng-files-ferc-permit-application-for-louisiana-export-facility). CLASSIFICATION: correct -- a short (3-mile) NGA-jurisdictional interconnecting lateral built to feed an LNG export terminal, not a gathering/production line; the direct GEM analogue to Plaquemines LNG's 'Gator Express' lateral (P0193, same staging batch). DUPLICATE: no sibling PID found on this batch's roster for the same short feed-gas lateral; not to be confused with the separate 'Commonwealth LNG Terminal' GEM facility record (gem.wiki/Commonwealth_LNG_Terminal), which is out of the pipeline tracker's scope. ATTRIBUTION: the FERC applicant/certificate holder is 'Commonwealth LNG, LLC' throughout the docket and the Federal Register notice; no separate 'Commonwealth LNG Pipeline, LLC' entity was found in FERC or Federal Register records (searched specifically -- see the Operator fill). MAJOR STATUS FINDING: this row is recorded Status=proposed, but Commonwealth LNG reached a positive Final Investment Decision and broke ground on May 15, 2026 (Caturus LLC PRNewswire release + KPLC Louisiana TV news coverage of the groundbreaking ceremony) -- see status_reviews below.

validity.recommendation: Update Diameter from 30 (in) to 42 (in). GEM's recorded 30in matches the pipeline's ORIGINAL 2019 application design (S&P Global's contemporaneous Aug 2019 article independently states the same 30-inch figure), but FERC's Final EIS (issued 2022) and FERC's current project-directory page both describe the AUTHORIZED, current design as 3.0 miles of 42-inch-diameter pipe, and offshore-technology.com's independent project profile confirms 42in. The design was apparently upsized between the 2019 filing and the 2022 FERC authorization.
validity.researcher_notes: Two independent sources describe the CURRENT/authorized diameter as 42-inch: FERC's own Final EIS news release (Wayback capture, https://web.archive.org/web/20220909160655/https://www.ferc.gov/news-events/news/ferc-staff-issues-final-environmental-impact-statement-commonwealth-lng-project: '3.0 miles of 42-inch-diameter pipeline') and FERC's project-directory page (Wayback capture, https://web.archive.org/web/20250321182833/https://www.ferc.gov/commonwealth-lng-project: '3-miles of 42-inch-diameter pipeline'), corroborated by offshore-technology.com (https://www.offshore-technology.com/projects/commonwealth-lng-terminal-louisiana-usa/: 'a three-mile ... pipeline with a diameter of 42in'). GEM's recorded value of 30in instead matches the ORIGINAL 2019 filing -- S&P Global's Aug 2019 article (Wayback capture, https://web.archive.org/web/20220420001722/https://www.spglobal.com/commodityinsights/en/market-insights/latest-news/natural-gas/082019-commonwealth-lng-files-ferc-permit-application-for-louisiana-export-facility) independently describes 'a 3.04 miles of 30-inch-diameter natural gas pipeline' at the time of the initial FERC application. Read together, these are not conflicting sources but two different points in the project's design history: 30in at the 2019 filing, 42in by the 2022 Final EIS/authorization onward. GEM's sheet still carries the superseded 2019-vintage figure. Diameter is a MISSING_REF unit (value present, ref cell empty); rather than add a ref that confirms the stale 30in figure, this is flagged as a spec concern with the corrected value recommended in `contested`, per the 'never force a wrong number just because it already sits in the cell' principle.

Ownership is genuinely ambiguous at the exact-entity level and NOT filled, per the 'never force a number' rule. What the FID press release actually states (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/caturus-announces-final-investment-decision-for-9-5-mtpa-commonwealth-lng-export-facility-in-cameron-la-302773264.html): Commonwealth LNG was originally developed under Kimmeridge Energy Management (Ben Dell, Kimmeridge Managing Partner, is Chairman of Commonwealth LNG); by the May 2026 FID, Commonwealth LNG sits inside a broader corporate platform called 'Caturus LLC,' alongside Caturus' separate upstream (E&P) operations. The release states 'Mubadala Energy...already holds a 24.1% stake in the CATURUS PLATFORM that includes Commonwealth LNG and Caturus' upstream operations' and 'Canada Pension Plan Investment Board (CPP Investments) will contribute $1.2 billion in financing to increase its total stake in the CATURUS PLATFORM to 31%' -- both percentages are explicitly stated at the PLATFORM level (Commonwealth LNG + separate upstream assets combined), not at the level of the Commonwealth LNG, LLC (or Commonwealth LNG Pipeline) entity itself. Other named financial participants -- EOC Partners, funds managed by BlackRock, and an Ares Infrastructure Opportunities Fund -- are described only as debt/financing partners, not named as equity owners with percentages. No source found breaks out Commonwealth LNG, LLC's (or this pipeline's) ownership on its own, separate from the Caturus platform aggregate. Filling Owner1-11%% with platform-level percentages would misattribute a system-wide figure to this specific entity/asset -- left UNRESOLVED with this detailed note rather than guessing an allocation.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: This row is badly stale at Status=proposed. On May 15, 2026, Caturus LLC (Commonwealth LNG's parent platform) announced a positive Final Investment Decision for the Commonwealth LNG project, including closing $9.75 billion in project financing (total commitments $21.25 billion) -- FID explicitly marks the start of full construction. Independently, KPLC (Louisiana TV news) covered the physical groundbreaking ceremony in Cameron Parish, attended by the U.S. Energy Secretary and Louisiana's Governor, corroborating that construction has visibly begun, not merely been financially authorized. Two independent origins (the company's own FID release and independent local TV news coverage of the physical groundbreaking) agree: recommend Status=construction, ConstructionYear=2026, ConstructionMonth=5, FIDStatus=FID. NOTE, not included above as a forced proposed_changes value: the project's startup/StartYear1 is NOT clearly resolved -- KPLC (https://www.kplctv.com/2026/05/16/13-billion-commonwealth-lng-breaks-ground-cameron-parish-with-energy-secretary-governor-hand/) attributes 'begin exporting LNG by 2029' to Commonwealth's own website, while the FID release itself (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/caturus-announces-final-investment-decision-for-9-5-mtpa-commonwealth-lng-export-facility-in-cameron-la-302773264.html) twice says operations commence in 2030. Since both figures trace back to Commonwealth/Caturus itself rather than being two independent confirmations of the same year, this is flagged here for awareness but intentionally left out of proposed_changes and out of the Start [ref] fill (see that fill's notes) rather than forcing either 2029 or 2030.
